open_points.subject: function purity, admission, and AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no clock, no randomness,” while the changed passage says withholding their standard-library entry points “is no guarantee against code written to get around it”; K-05 calls admission “a deterministic verdict,” and M08 says a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same value.
open_points.question: Is absence of clock and randomness a required invariant whose circumvention must prevent admission, or is it only a best-effort restriction under which an admitted implementation may observe time or randomness; if the latter, can the same implementation and corpus have different admission verdicts despite M08's value identity?
options: Circumventing access is prohibited and any implementation that obtains clock or randomness must be refused.
Only standard-library access is withheld; circumvention may execute, so admission results can vary and M08's identity/lifecycle must represent distinct verdicts.
Only standard-library access is withheld, but the kernel still treats one computed verdict as authoritative for that implementation and corpus despite possible non-reproducibility.
open_points.default_guess: Treat no-clock and no-randomness as a normative invariant and refuse an implementation whenever circumvention is detected, while acknowledging that the stated mechanism cannot guarantee detection.

witness.initial: A contract version has one trial case with a fixed expected output; an implementation for it obtains randomness through code that bypasses the standard library's guarded entry point.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation, causing the kernel to run admission over the corpus.
The same agent later submits the equal implementation again while the corpus is unchanged, causing admission to run the cases again as M08 specifies.
outcomes: The no-randomness rule is an invariant, so the bypass is a sandbox violation and both submissions are refused.

The new caveat makes the restriction best-effort, so the bypass runs; one admission can match the expected output and admit while the other mismatches and refuses, although M08 identifies both as the same verdict value for the same implementation and corpus.
witness.observer: The authoring agent sees different admission results and whether the implementation is activated; later flow runners see whether that implementation can be pinned.
